item.title: Ser vs. Estar and the Present Tense
item.description: Lesson 3: Ser vs. Estar and the Present Tense This lesson tackles the two most important verbs in Spanish — ser and estar, both meaning 'to be' — plus the present tense, which lets you describe what you do every day. English uses one 'to be' for everything; Spanish splits the job in two, and mixing…

item.title: Numbers, Time, Days — The Everyday Vocabulary Core
item.description: Lesson 4: Numbers, Time, Days — The Everyday Vocabulary Core This lesson builds your everyday number vocabulary: counting, telling time, and using days, months, and dates. Numbers are pure utility — prices, phone numbers, addresses, schedules — and telling the time unlocks appointments, opening…

item.title: Asking Questions — Directions, Shopping, and Small-Talk Dialogues
item.description: Lesson 5: Asking Questions — Directions, Shopping, and Small-Talk Dialogues This lesson turns you into someone who can get answers: how to form every kind of question, ask for directions, handle a full shopping conversation, and keep small talk going. item.title: Talking About the Past — The Preterite Tense
item.description: Lesson 6: Talking About the Past — The Preterite Tense This lesson gives you the past tense — the preterite — so you can say what you did, where you went, and what happened. Without a past tense you are stuck in the eternal present; with it, you can tell stories, explain your day, and answer the…
